20-Year-Old Drives Rare Chevy Caprice, Wants Everything Impala SS on It, Says It Won't Be a Clone
14 photos
Photo: Pomeroy's Garage | YouTube
A young man from Ontario bought a rust-free, rare 1996 Chevrolet Caprice B4U. While it might be the kind of car that a grandma would drive, he loves the attention that the classic sedan brings him. Because he loves Impala SSs, he plans to swap a thing or two (or more), but promises: "I won't turn it into an Impala SS clone!"
Young people usually chase after the newest cars with the latest tech. This guy, however, is into classic cars and hunts the best deals. John Pomeroy , who is only 20 years old, drives cars that are sometimes double his age or more.
His latest purchase is a 30-year-old Chevy Caprice B4U he bought for $5,000 CAD, which translates to roughly US$3,490. " An amazing steal ," he says. That’s not entirely true. While low-mileage, well-preserved examples can fetch around US$10,000 at auctions, cars that are not exactly garage queens rarely go over the US $5,000 mark.
However, he is going to spend some more money on a makeover. He absolutely loves Chevy Impala SSs and plans to make the Caprice a bit sportier without turning it into an Impala SS clone. That sounds like a promise he won’t be able to keep.
Photo: Pomeroy's Garage | YouTube The B4U is a rare, factory-optioned performance package that gave the Caprice sedans the mechanical hardware of the iconic Impala SS without the sporty appearance, making it the ultimate sleeper. Unofficial reports indicate that roughly 9,064 B4U Chevy Caprices were built for the model year
While the 1994 - 1996 Impala SS featured monochromatic paint, a rear spoiler, bucket seats, and 17-inch wheels, a B4U Caprice kept its chrome trim, wire hubcaps or standard alloys, hood ornament, and front bench seat.
Because the Impala SS and the Chevy Caprice B4U shared the exact same LT1 and heavy-duty underpinnings, the Caprice delivered nearly identical acceleration and highway cruising power at a fraction of the price of the Impala SS.
1996 was the final year of the fourth-generation B-body Caprice. That year, ordering the B4U option was the only way to get the range-topping powertrain in a non-police civilian sedan. In addition to the LT1 V8, the car came with the FE3 sport suspension, the V08 heavy-duty cooling, a limited-slip differential, and a dual exhaust system.
Photo: Pomeroy's Garage | YouTube He bought the body-on-frame sedan out of Texas, so it comes rust-free, has never even been driven in winter, and has never seen salt. Things are probably about to change in Ontario, Canada, where Pomeroy lives, but he plans to take care of it so that it drives 30 more years.
Finished in Adriatic Blue, which John says is one of his all-time favorite colors, along with black and white on these Caprices. It came with minor dings and dents, but overall, it is in great condition, considering its age, and has some of the most desirable features of its era.
The Caprice B4U rides on Impala five-spoke Chevy Impala wheels, but Pomeroy would love a set of N97 9C1s. However, he is going to swap them for OZ Racing wheels that he used to have on his 1985 Buick LeSabre. An Impala trunk lid with a little spoiler will replace the original one.
The factory taillights will be out, and Impala units will be in. John also intends to switch to an Impala SS rear end with disc brakes all around and plans to get rid of the purple rear window tints. Those tints protect a cabin that is in far worse condition than the exterior, which is far from abnormal at 123,000 miles (197,949 kilometers).
Photo: Pomeroy's Garage | YouTube The leather steering wheel is peeling off, and the driver’s seat is split open. The dashboard is cracked, but the new owner has a spare one to replace the factory dash. The good news that the door panels are in good condition. Everything works on board.
The 1996 Caprice features power seats, power mirrors, and the very rare optional Twilight Sentinel, General Motors' automatic headlight and exit-lighting system, which automatically turns the exterior lights on at dusk, turns them off in bright daylight, and keeps them lit briefly after the driver parks it so that they can walk to their door at night.
Pomeroy is planning to replace the factory seats with Bonneville seats up front and Impala seats out back. As for the cargo space, " t his is a seven-body trunk ," says the new owner of the Caprice. He probably watched too many crime movies.
At the opposite end, under the long hood, which John wants to replace with an SLP Ram Air hood, sits the 5.7-liter LT1 V8, derived from the Corvette . The V8 produces 260 horsepower (264 metric horsepower) and 330 pound-feet (447 Newton meters) of torque. That makes it accelerate from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 7.2 seconds on its way to a top speed of 135 mph (217 kph).
With everything he plans to modify on the car, it doesn’t sound like a Chevy Impala SS clone. It sounds like the Impala SS itself.
